def predict(probe):
    # Rule: strip leading whitespace (incl. unicode), then append "ny" [E2, E4, E6, E8]
    # Trailing whitespace preserved [E4, E6, E8]
    # Internal whitespace preserved [E4, E10]
    # No case change, no other edits [E1, E5, E9]
    # \u00a0 counts as leading whitespace [E8]
    # Empty string -> "ny" [E2]
    inputs = probe.get("inputs", [])
    outputs = []
    for s in inputs:
        if not isinstance(s, str):
            s = str(s)
        outputs.append(s.lstrip() + "ny")
    return {"outputs": outputs}
notes: The box strips all leading whitespace (including Unicode like `\u00a0`) from the input, then appends the literal string `"ny"`, preserving everything else (case, internal spaces, trailing whitespace).
